These fixtures are **simulated Gemini CLI JSON reports**, not billed model runs. They exercise successful, failed, missing, partial, interrupted and malformed output. Empty `interrupted.json` represents cancellation before the CLI emits its terminal JSON report; execution tests separately cover cancellation and timeout status.

Schema provenance, inspected 2026-10-19: installed `@google/gemini-cli` 0.43.0, `bundle/chunk-QH43L44B.js`, source sections `packages/core/src/output/json-formatter.ts`, `packages/core/src/telemetry/uiTelemetry.ts`, and `packages/core/src/telemetry/types.ts`; `bundle/gemini-PBHAWQU6.js` headless output and error handling. Public references: https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/headless/ and https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content#UsageMetadata.

The adapter uses `--output-format json`: its `stats.models[model].tokens` includes `prompt`, `candidates`, `thoughts`, `tool`, `total`, `cached`, and `input`. In CLI 0.43.0, stream JSON drops `thoughts`, so it cannot support complete output accounting. Native `prompt` includes cached tokens; `input` means `prompt-cached`. The API defines `total` as `prompt+tool+candidates+thoughts`. Normalize input as `prompt+tool` and output as `candidates+thoughts`, preserve cache and thoughts as subsets, and require the native total to reconcile. API request and error counters are retained per model. Any API error makes normalized usage unknown, including a successful retry: CLI `processApiError` increments counters without adding usage, so token totals can omit failed requests. Missing API counters and zero-request reports also remain incomplete; contradictory counters are rejected. Missing primary fields remain unknown; missing cache detail is optional. Per-role counters repeat per-model data and are never added again.

These are **CLI-reported** counts. The CLI internally defaults absent API metadata to zero, so a reported zero cannot prove the provider supplied a zero or that billing is complete. API/provider invoice reconciliation remains a live-pilot check. Multiple reported model identifiers are retained for the runner's fixed-model check; they do not prove a specific backend revision. No backend model or reasoning setting is inferred. Tool names come only from native tool counters, not configuration; an absent tool report stays unknown. Tool errors can still be completed invocations.

The JSON mode has one terminal report, not a streamed lifecycle history. Missing final output loses intermediate usage, which remains unknown and stops budgeted execution. Warnings are retained, and a terminal error retains any reported usage. The failure fixture includes counts to exercise retention even though the CLI's `formatError` path commonly omits stats. Fixtures establish parser behavior, not live compatibility.
